letters.sound: j (plain): soft and relaxed, with only a little breath
letters.as: Close to the "j" in "jam," but softer. At the start of a word it can sound like a very light "ch" with almost no air.

letters.sound: ch (aspirated): comes with a strong puff of air
letters.as: Close to the "ch" in "church." Push out a clear burst of breath.

letters.sound: jj (tense): tight, sharp, and with no puff of air
letters.as: No exact English match. Think of the "tch" in "pitch," but tighten your throat and tongue and let out no breath.

objective: Beginner learners will tell apart and say word-initial ㅈ (plain), ㅊ (aspirated) and ㅉ (tense), then choose the right word in the sets 자다/차다/짜다 and 지다/치다/찌다.
summary: Learn how ㅈ, ㅊ and ㅉ sound at the start of a word. They differ in breath and tension. Use them to pick the right verb in sets like 자다/차다/짜다 and 지다/치다/찌다.
